finding: Anthropic, Cohere and Bedrock could discard native-tool blocks/payloads and still return accompanying prose as a successful completion.
change: Anthropic rejects native tool-use/result block families and tool_use/pause_turn before text or refusal projection.
Cohere retains tool_calls and rejects nonempty payloads or TOOL_CALL finish reasons before projecting text.
Bedrock retains toolUse/toolResult and rejects their presence or tool_use before the shared production text/refusal projection.
coverage: Eight new registered tests: native client/server tools, result blocks, marker-only responses, malformed payloads and refusal conflicts; ordinary text/thinking/refusal compatibility; Anthropic and Cohere real mocked HTTP complete and buffered-stream failures with exact payload-free errors and request counts. Bedrock uses the same decoder/projection helper as production; no live AWS or signing claim.
review: GPT-6.1 Terra high prompt-only review of supplied core implementation and test description; no concrete remaining finding. Root performed bounded text/diff inspection.
limits: No native tool execution or new streaming transport. Existing permissions, cost/WAL/effect gates, response bounds and credential handling unchanged.

Gemini currently requires text in each part and rejects protocol-valid standalone function-call parts during bounded decoding; this slice neither changes that schema nor claims every malformed or future Gemini block is covered.
Whole A08 transport/cancellation parity, current-producer native tests and release acceptance remain open.
